ORDER BY oc.HIERARCHY_TYPE ASC

rows.question: For each course, list its title, name of the building of the course location, duration (in terms of days), and a running average of the duration (in terms of days) using a window of two preceding and two following courses (partitioned by academic year and sorted by course start date).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH term_dates AS (
  SELECT
    at.TERM_CODE,
    at.TERM_START_DATE,
    at.TERM_END_DATE
  FROM academic_terms at
  UNION
  SELECT
    ata.TERM_CODE,
    ata.TERM_START_DATE,
    ata.TERM_END_DATE
  FROM academic_terms_all ata
),
courses AS (
  SELECT
    so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
    so.SUBJECT_KEY,
    so.TERM_CODE,
    -- choose academic year from cis, then ccso, then dr
    COALESCE(cis.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR, dr.ACADEMIC_YEAR) AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    -- choose title preferring cis, then ccso, then dr
    COALESCE(NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(ccso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(dr.SUBJECT_TITLE, '')) AS course_title,
    -- canonical term start/end from term_dates (prefer course row TERM if present? question prefers term tables; use term_dates joined by TERM_CODE)
    td.TERM_START_DATE,
    td.TERM_END_DATE,
    -- parse start/end as DATE for ordering and calculations
    STR_TO_DATE(td.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') AS term_start_date_parsed,
    STR_TO_DATE(td.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') AS term_end_date_parsed,
    -- meet place to join to buildings
    so.MEET_PLACE
  FROM subject_offered so
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
    ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
  LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered ccso
    ON ccso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID AND ccso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dr
    ON dr.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID AND dr.SO_TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  LEFT JOIN term_dates td
    ON td.TERM_CODE = COALESCE(so.TERM_CODE, ccso.TERM_CODE, dr.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE)
  WHERE
    -- require parsable start and end dates present in term_dates
    td.TERM_START_DATE IS NOT NULL
    AND td.TERM_END_DATE IS NOT NULL
    AND STR_TO_DATE(td.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
    AND STR_TO_DATE(td.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
    -- require a non-null title
    AND COALESCE(NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(ccso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(dr.SUBJECT_TITLE, '')) IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  c.course_title AS course_title,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
  -- duration: non-inclusive difference as requested: date(end) - date(start)
  DATEDIFF(c.term_end_date_parsed, c.term_start_date_parsed) AS duration_days,
  -- running average over window of 2 preceding and 2 following within same academic year ordered by term start date
  AVG(DATEDIFF(c.term_end_date_parsed, c.term_start_date_parsed)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY c.ACADEMIC_YEAR
    ORDER BY c.term_start_date_parsed
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING
  ) AS running_avg_duration_days
FROM courses c
JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = c.MEET_PLACE
ORDER BY
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR ASC,
  c.term_start_date_parsed ASC

rows.question: For each course, list its name, name of the building of the course location, the start date, the name of the course before it, and the name of the course after it, access level of the building, and the assignable area of the room used for the course, sorted by the ascending order start date and course name.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, cs.SUBJECT_TITLE, dc.SUBJECT_TITLE, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS course_name,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
  atbl.TERM_START_DATE AS start_date,
  LAG(COALESCE(ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, cs.SUBJECT_TITLE, dc.SUBJECT_TITLE, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE))
    OVER (ORDER BY atbl.TERM_START_DATE ASC, COALESCE(ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, cs.SUBJECT_TITLE, dc.SUBJECT_TITLE, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE) ASC) AS previous_course,
  LEAD(COALESCE(ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, cs.SUBJECT_TITLE, dc.SUBJECT_TITLE, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE))
    OVER (ORDER BY atbl.TERM_START_DATE ASC, COALESCE(ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, cs.SUBJECT_TITLE, dc.SUBJECT_TITLE, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE) ASC) AS following_course,
  COALESCE(fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME, fr.ACCESS_LEVEL, fclt.ACCESS_LEVEL) AS building_access_level,
  COALESCE(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, fr.AREA, fclt.AREA) AS room_assignable_area
FROM academic_terms atbl
LEFT JOIN subject_summary ss
  ON ss.TERM_CODE = atbl.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cs
  ON cs.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dc
  ON dc.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lso.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID AND lso.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so
  ON so.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE
  AND so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID
-- match fac_rooms by SPACE_ID or ROOM: perform two LEFT JOINs and coalesce results
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr_by_space
  ON fr_by_space.SPACE_ID IS NOT NULL AND fr_by_space.SPACE_ID = so.MEET_PLACE
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr_by_room
  ON fr_by_room.ROOM IS NOT NULL AND fr_by_room.ROOM = so.MEET_PLACE
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    fr_space.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
    fr_space.BUILDING_KEY,
    fr_space.FLOOR,
    fr_space.ROOM,
    fr_space.SPACE_ID,
    fr_space.MAJOR_USE_KEY,
    fr_space.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
    fr_space.USE_KEY,
    fr_space.USE_DESC,
    fr_space.MINOR_USE_KEY,
    fr_space.MINOR_USE_DESC,
    fr_space.ORGANIZATION_KEY,
    fr_space.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
    fr_space.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY,
    fr_space.MINOR_ORGANIZATION,
    fr_space.AREA,
    fr_space.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
    fr_space.DEPT_CODE,
    fr_space.ACCESS_LEVEL
  FROM fac_rooms fr_space
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    fr_room.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
    fr_room.BUILDING_KEY,
    fr_room.FLOOR,
    fr_room.ROOM,
    fr_room.SPACE_ID,
    fr_room.MAJOR_USE_KEY,
    fr_room.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
    fr_room.USE_KEY,
    fr_room.USE_DESC,
    fr_room.MINOR_USE_KEY,
    fr_room.MINOR_USE_DESC,
    fr_room.ORGANIZATION_KEY,
    fr_room.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
    fr_room.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY,
    fr_room.MINOR_ORGANIZATION,
    fr_room.AREA,
    fr_room.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
    fr_room.DEPT_CODE,
    fr_room.ACCESS_LEVEL
  FROM fac_rooms fr_room
) fr ON (fr.SPACE_ID IS NOT NULL AND fr.SPACE_ID = so.MEET_PLACE)
     OR (fr.ROOM IS NOT NULL AND fr.ROOM = so.MEET_PLACE)
-- fclt_rooms: join similarly using a derived for simplicity
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    fclt.FCLT_ROOM_KEY,
    fclt.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
    fclt.FLOOR,
    fclt.ROOM,
    fclt.SPACE_ID,
    fclt.AREA,
    fclt.ACCESS_LEVEL
  FROM fclt_rooms fclt
) fclt ON (fclt.SPACE_ID IS NOT NULL AND fclt.SPACE_ID = so.MEET_PLACE)
       OR (fclt.ROOM IS NOT NULL AND fclt.ROOM = so.MEET_PLACE)
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = COALESCE(fr.BUILDING_KEY, fclt.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY)
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = COALESCE(fr.BUILDING_KEY, fclt.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY)
     AND ff.FLOOR = COALESCE(fr.FLOOR, fclt.FLOOR)
WHERE atbl.TERM_START_DATE IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY atbl.TERM_START_DATE ASC, course_name ASC

rows.question: For email lists with names starting with e (case insensitive), containing 10 to 20 members inclusive, and where over 75% are computer science students, provide the list name, owner, and member count.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH moira_lists_core AS (
  SELECT
    ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
    mlo.OWNER AS owner
  FROM moira_list ml
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_owner mlo
    ON mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
),
member_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS member_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN opc.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dept6_count
  FROM moira_list_detail md
  LEFT JOIN opa_person_current opc
    ON md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = opc.MIT_ID
  GROUP BY md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
)
SELECT
  mlc.list_name,
  mlc.owner,
  ma.member_count
FROM moira_lists_core mlc
JOIN member_aggregates ma
  ON mlc.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ma.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
WHERE LOWER(mlc.list_name) LIKE 'e%'
  AND ma.member_count BETWEEN 10 AND 20
  AND (ma.dept6_count / ma.member_count) > 0.75

rows.question: For students with last names starting with K, list their names, the phone numbers of departments they belong to, total number of mailing lists each student is in, and the average size of the mailing lists each student is in.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH student_departments AS (
  SELECT
    mit.FULL_NAME                               AS full_name,
    mit.DEPARTMENT                              AS department_code,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '') = '' 
           AND COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') = '' THEN NULL
      WHEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '') = '' THEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER
      WHEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') = '' THEN NULL
      ELSE CONCAT(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '-', sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER)
    END                                         AS phone_number
  FROM mit_student_directory AS mit
  LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department AS sad
    ON mit.DEPARTMENT = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
  WHERE mit.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
),
moira_list_sizes AS (
  SELECT
    m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY                            AS list_key,
    m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME                           AS list_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER)         AS member_count
  FROM moira_list m
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail d
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
  GROUP BY m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY, m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME
),
moira_list_memberships AS (
  SELECT
    mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID                AS member_mit_id,
    mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY                          AS list_key
  FROM moira_list_detail mld
  WHERE mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  s.FULL_NAME                                  AS name,
  COALESCE(sd.department_phone_numbers, '')    AS department_phone_numbers,
  COALESCE(m.mail_count, 0)                    AS mailing_list_count,
  COALESCE(m.avg_list_size, 0)                 AS average_mailing_list_size
FROM mit_student_directory s
LEFT JOIN (
  -- aggregate phone numbers for the student's department(s)
  SELECT
    sd.full_name,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT sd.phone_number ORDER BY sd.phone_number SEPARATOR ',') AS department_phone_numbers
  FROM student_departments sd
  GROUP BY sd.full_name
) sd ON s.FULL_NAME = sd.full_name
LEFT JOIN (
  -- per-student mailing list counts and average list sizes
  SELECT
    ml.member_mit_id AS member_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ml.list_key) AS mail_count,
    AVG(mzs.member_count) AS avg_list_size
  FROM moira_list_memberships ml
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_sizes mzs
    ON ml.list_key = mzs.list_key
  GROUP BY ml.member_mit_id
) m ON s.FULL_NAME = m.member_id
WHERE s.LAST_NAME LIKE 'K%'
ORDER BY s.LAST_NAME, s.FIRST_NAME

rows.question: From the 100 email lists with the most number of subscribers, list their names, their total number of subscribers, their public status, the name of the department with the most presence in the list, and the number of students from this department in the list.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH directory_person_primary_department AS (
  -- Map people (by name as recorded in moira_list_detail) to their primary department using OPA/SIS and FAC organization links.
  -- Carry person identifier so joins remain joinable in downstream CTEs.
  SELECT
    opc.MIT_ID AS PERSON_ID,
    opc.FULL_NAME AS PRINCIPAL_NAME,
    opc.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    opc.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
  FROM opa_person_current opc
),
moira_list_subscribers AS (
  -- All subscribers on MOIRA-managed lists (join list_detail -> list ensures we consider MOIRA lists present in moira_list).
  SELECT
    md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS ML_ID,
    m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS ML_NAME,
    md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS MEMBER_PRINCIPAL,
    m.IS_PUBLIC AS IS_PUBLIC,
    md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MEMBER_MIT_ID
  FROM moira_list_detail md
  JOIN moira_list m
    ON md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
),
-- Attach department information to each subscriber where possible. Prefer MIT_ID match if available, else match by principal/full name.
subscribers_with_dept AS (
  SELECT
    s.ML_ID,
    s.ML_NAME,
    s.IS_PUBLIC,
    s.MEMBER_PRINCIPAL,
    s.MEMBER_MIT_ID,
    COALESCE(d.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, NULL) AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    -- Flag whether this subscriber is a student. There is no explicit SIS student flag in provided schema;
    -- we attempt to infer student status via presence in student-degree-related tables is not possible with given schema.
    -- Because the schema does not include a clear student flag, we cannot reliably mark students. Set NULL so caller knows it's unavailable.
    NULL AS IS_STUDENT_FLAG
  FROM moira_list_subscribers s
  LEFT JOIN directory_person_primary_department d
    ON (s.MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND s.MEMBER_MIT_ID <> '' AND d.PERSON_ID = s.MEMBER_MIT_ID)
       OR (s.MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NULL OR s.MEMBER_MIT_ID = '') AND d.PRINCIPAL_NAME = s.MEMBER_PRINCIPAL
),
-- Count members per (list, department)
list_dept_counts AS (
  SELECT
    ML_ID,
    ML_NAME,
    IS_PUBLIC,
    COALESCE(HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, 'Unknown') AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    COUNT(*) AS dept_member_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN IS_STUDENT_FLAG = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dept_student_count
  FROM subscribers_with_dept
  GROUP BY ML_ID, ML_NAME, IS_PUBLIC, COALESCE(HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, 'Unknown')
),
-- Total subscribers per list
list_totals AS (
  SELECT
    ML_ID,
    ML_NAME,
    IS_PUBLIC,
    SUM(dept_member_count) AS total_subscribers
  FROM list_dept_counts
  GROUP BY ML_ID, ML_NAME, IS_PUBLIC
),
-- For each list find the department with the largest member count. Break ties by department name.
list_top_department AS (
  SELECT
    ldc.ML_ID,
    ldc.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS top_department_name,
    ldc.dept_member_count,
    ldc.dept_student_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ldc.ML_ID ORDER BY ldc.dept_member_count DESC, ldc.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME ASC) AS rn
  FROM list_dept_counts ldc
)
SELECT
  lt.ML_NAME AS list_name,
  CAST(lt.total_subscribers AS UNSIGNED) AS total_subscribers,
  lt.IS_PUBLIC AS is_public,
  COALESCE(ltd.top_department_name, 'Unknown') AS top_department_name,
  CAST(COALESCE(ltd.dept_student_count, 0) AS UNSIGNED) AS top_department_student_count
FROM list_totals lt
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ML_ID, top_department_name, dept_student_count
  FROM list_top_department
  WHERE rn = 1
) ltd
  ON lt.ML_ID = ltd.ML_ID
ORDER BY lt.total_subscribers DESC
LIMIT 100

rows.question: Calculate the total assignable and non-assignable area for each building by summing up the respective areas of all its floors. For each building, list the building name, building number, total assignable area, total non-assignable area, and total room count, sorted in descending order of the total assignable area.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH building_core_198 AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
    b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
  FROM buildings b
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COALESCE(ff.total_assignable_area, 0) AS TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  COALESCE(ff.total_non_assignable_area, 0) AS TOTAL_NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  COALESCE(fb.total_room_count, 0) AS TOTAL_ROOM_COUNT
FROM building_core_198 b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    SUM(COALESCE(ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0)) AS total_assignable_area,
    SUM(COALESCE(EXT_GROSS_AREA, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0)) AS total_non_assignable_area
  FROM fac_floor
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
) ff
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = ff.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_NUMBER,
    SUM(COALESCE(NUM_OF_ROOMS, 0)) AS total_room_count
  FROM fac_building
  GROUP BY BUILDING_NUMBER
) fb
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
ORDER BY TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA DESC

rows.question: List all rooms in building 45, including their full name, area, major use, the organization that occupies them, the count of rooms per major use, and the total area occupied by rooms for each organization.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH organization_lookup_201 AS (
  SELECT
    fo.`ORGANIZATION_KEY` AS `ORGANIZATION_KEY`,
    fo.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`
  FROM `fac_organization` fo
),
building_rooms_core AS (
  SELECT
    `FAC_ROOM_KEY`      AS ROOM_KEY,
    `ROOM`              AS ROOM_IDENTIFIER,
    `ROOM_FULL_NAME`    AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
    `AREA`              AS ROOM_AREA,
    `MAJOR_USE_KEY`     AS MAJOR_USE_KEY,
    `ORGANIZATION_KEY`  AS ORGANIZATION_KEY,
    `BUILDING_KEY`      AS BUILDING_KEY
  FROM `fac_rooms`
),
major_use_lookup AS (
  SELECT
    `MAJOR_USE_KEY` AS MAJOR_USE_KEY,
    `MAJOR_USE`     AS MAJOR_USE
  FROM `fac_major_use`
)
SELECT
  br.ROOM_KEY                       AS ROOM_IDENTIFIER,
  br.ROOM_FULL_NAME                 AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  br.ROOM_AREA                      AS ROOM_AREA,
  mu.MAJOR_USE                      AS MAJOR_USE,
  org.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME            AS OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mu.MAJOR_USE) 
                                    AS ROOMS_PER_MAJOR_USE,
  SUM(br.ROOM_AREA) OVER (PARTITION BY org.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME) 
                                    AS TOTAL_AREA_PER_ORGANIZATION
FROM building_rooms_core AS br
LEFT JOIN major_use_lookup AS mu
  ON br.MAJOR_USE_KEY = mu.MAJOR_USE_KEY
LEFT JOIN organization_lookup_201 AS org
  ON br.ORGANIZATION_KEY = org.ORGANIZATION_KEY
WHERE br.BUILDING_KEY = '45'
  AND br.ROOM_AREA IS NOT NULL
  AND mu.MAJOR_USE IS NOT NULL
  AND mu.MAJOR_USE <> ''
  AND org.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND org.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME <> ''
ORDER BY br.ROOM_KEY

rows.question: List the name, number, construction date, and type of all buildings, along with the count of addresses associated with each building, the average gross area of the buildings, and the total number of rooms in each building. Sort the results by building name.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH addr_counts AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_KEY,
    -- count non-null/non-empty of BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS and BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS on buildings table
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    +
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    AS ADDRESS_COUNT
  FROM buildings b
),
avg_gross AS (
  -- single scalar value repeated for every row: average of BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE across all buildings
  SELECT AVG(BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS AVG_GROSS_SQFT FROM buildings
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- construction date not present in buildings schema; return NULL per instructions
  NULL AS CONSTRUCTION_DATE,
  -- BUILDING_TYPE not present on buildings; return NULL (could join fclt_building if desired, but spec allows NULL)
  NULL AS BUILDING_TYPE,
  COALESCE(a.ADDRESS_COUNT, 0) AS ADDRESS_COUNT,
  ag.AVG_GROSS_SQFT AS AVG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- total number of rooms: use BUILDING_COUNTER or NUM_OF_ROOMS if available; buildings has BUILDING_COUNTER column.
  -- The schema includes BUILDING_COUNTER and not explicit total rooms; use BUILDING_COUNTER as TOTAL_ROOMS.
  COALESCE(b.BUILDING_COUNTER, 0) AS TOTAL_ROOMS
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN addr_counts a
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = a.BUILDING_KEY
CROSS JOIN avg_gross ag
ORDER BY b.BUILDING_NAME ASC

rows.question: For each department, list its name, number of unique courses offered, the number of unique reserved materials, and the number of unique instructors associated with those courses, sorted by the number of unique courses offered in descending order.

WITH course_reserved_materials AS (
SELECT
  /* from library_reserve_matrl_detail: use provided keys/columns as-is and alias to requested names */
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,

  library_reserve_matrl_detail.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE_matrl,
  /* Requested output columns: these must come from the exact tables named in the spec.
     The schema does not contain columns named RESERVE_ID or RESERVE_TITLE in library_reserve_matrl_detail,
     so we must attempt to obtain them by joining the library_reserve_catalog table where appropriate.
     According to the developer instruction, lift question-specific literals out of the view.
     Here we expose the catalog's identifying fields (system number/title) as the RESERVE_* outputs. */
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS RESERVE_ID,

     The table library_subject_offered contains SUBJECT_ID and various course number fields.
     Use exact columns from that table and alias them as requested. */
  library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  library_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  library_subject_offered.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  /* Carry through keys so view remains joinable to parents */
  library_subject_offered.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY_from_subject,
  library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY_from_catalog,
  /* Provide a derived coalesced grain column as requested in the grain definition:
     coalesce(library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID, (library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_CODE || '|' || library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_NUMBER))
     MySQL uses CONCAT and COALESCE; however the grain definition mandates the expression.
     Expose it as SUBJECT_GRAIN. */
  COALESCE(
    library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
    CONCAT(library_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, '|', library_subject_offered.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
  ) AS SUBJECT_GRAIN
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail
  /* Join to catalog to obtain RESERVE_TITLE and preserve catalog key relationships.
     Use LEFT JOIN so that if no catalog exists the relation still appears with NULLs. */
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  /* Join to subject offered to obtain subject identifiers and course numbering.
     LEFT JOIN so that if no subject row exists the reserve-to-course relation still appears (subject columns NULL). */
  LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = library_subject_offered.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
),
catalog_course_identifiers AS (
SELECT
  c.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM
  cis_course_catalog c
),
department_list_from_catalogs AS (
SELECT
  DISTINCT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog`
WHERE
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` <> ''
),
course_instructors AS (
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_MIT_ID,
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_NAME,
  lso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  lso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  lso.`MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER
FROM `library_course_instructor` lci
JOIN `library_subject_offered` lso
  ON (
       (lci.`UNIT` IS NOT NULL AND lci.`UNIT` = lso.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE`)
       OR (lci.`DEPARTMENT` IS NOT NULL AND lci.`DEPARTMENT` = lso.`OFFER_DEPT_NAME`)
     )
)
SELECT
  d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name,
  d.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS department_id,
  COALESCE(c.unique_courses, 0) AS unique_courses,
  COALESCE(r.unique_reserved_materials, 0) AS unique_reserved_materials,
  COALESCE(i.unique_instructors, 0) AS unique_instructors
FROM department_list_from_catalogs d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    COUNT(DISTINCT SUBJECT_ID) AS unique_courses
  FROM catalog_course_identifiers
  GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE
) c ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN (
  -- map reserved materials to departments via catalog_course_identifiers and count distinct reserves per department
  SELECT
    cci.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    COUNT(DISTINCT crm.RESERVE_ID) AS unique_reserved_materials
  FROM course_reserved_materials crm
  JOIN catalog_course_identifiers cci
    ON ( (crm.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND cci.SUBJECT_ID = crm.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (crm.SUBJECT_ID IS NULL AND cci.SUBJECT_CODE = crm.SUBJECT_CODE AND cci.SUBJECT_NUMBER = crm.SUBJECT_NUMBER) )
  GROUP BY cci.DEPARTMENT_CODE
) r ON r.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN (
  -- map instructors to departments via catalog_course_identifiers and count distinct instructors per department
  SELECT
    cci.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ci.INSTRUCTOR_MIT_ID) AS unique_instructors
  FROM course_instructors ci
  JOIN catalog_course_identifiers cci
    ON ( (ci.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND cci.SUBJECT_ID = ci.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (ci.SUBJECT_ID IS NULL AND cci.SUBJECT_CODE = ci.SUBJECT_CODE AND cci.SUBJECT_NUMBER = ci.SUBJECT_NUMBER) )
  GROUP BY cci.DEPARTMENT_CODE
) i ON i.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
ORDER BY unique_courses DESC

rows.question: For each course title, list the title, the total number of reserved materials, and the count of distinct material status associated with those materials, sorted by the total number of reserved materials in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH course_titles AS (
SELECT
  `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  TRIM(BOTH ' ' FROM NULLIF(`subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, '')) AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`
FROM
  `subject_offered`
),
materials_joined_to_courses AS (
SELECT
  lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS MTRL_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS RESERVE_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY AS MTRL_STATUS,
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.COURSE_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  so.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd
LEFT JOIN
  library_subject_offered AS lso
    ON lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
    AND (lmd.TERM_CODE IS NULL OR lmd.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE)
LEFT JOIN
  subject_offered AS so
    /* prefer direct match via subject_offered key from library_subject_offered when available */
    ON (
         (lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (lso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (lso.COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER)
       )
    /* further restrict by TERM_CODE when present in both */
    AND (lso.TERM_CODE IS NULL OR lso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE)
WHERE
  -- base grain is one reserved-material record; include all material rows (use LEFT JOINs above)
  1 = 1
),
reserved_materials_clean AS (
SELECT
  lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`            AS MTRL_ID,
  lmd.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`          AS RESERVE_ID,
  lmd.`SUBJECT_ID`                              AS SUBJECT_ID,
  lmd.`TERM_CODE`                                AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  lmd.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`             AS SECTION_ID,
  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`                 AS MTRL_STATUS
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lmd
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
    ON lmd.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows with missing material identifier(s)
  lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` <> ''
  -- exclude rows with missing reserve/course key (keeps joinable grain)
  AND lmd.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND lmd.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` <> ''
)
SELECT
  subject_title AS course_title,
  COUNT(*) AS total_reserved_materials,
  COUNT(DISTINCT MTRL_STATUS) AS distinct_material_status_count
FROM materials_joined_to_courses
WHERE subject_title IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(subject_title) <> ''
GROUP BY subject_title
ORDER BY total_reserved_materials DESC

rows.question: For each instructor, list their name, the number of unique courses they teach, the total number of material assignments, average publication year, and number of distinct status, sorted by the number of unique courses in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH instructor_identity AS (
  SELECT
    opc.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE AS kerb,
    opc.FULL_NAME AS display_name
  FROM opa_person_current opc
  WHERE opc.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE IS NOT NULL
    AND opc.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE <> ''
    AND (opc.IS_OPA_REQUIRED = 'Y' OR opc.IS_FACULTY = 'Y' OR opc.ADMIN_EMPLOYEE_TYPE IS NOT NULL)
  GROUP BY opc.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE, opc.FULL_NAME
),
instructor_materials_link AS (
  SELECT
    lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS kerb,
    lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS material_id,
    lrc.CATALOG_YEAR AS pub_year,
    lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE AS status_code,
    lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS library_course_instructor_id,
    lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS library_reserve_matrl_detail_id
  FROM library_course_instructor lci
  JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lmd
    ON lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
    ON lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
    ON lmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
),
instructor_course_assignments AS (
  SELECT
    lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS kerb,
    so.SUBJECT_ID AS subject_id,
    cc.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS catalog_year,
    cc.SUBJECT_CODE AS subject_label,
    cc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS catalog_number,
    cc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS title,
    lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS id
  FROM library_course_instructor lci
  JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
    ON lrmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
  JOIN library_subject_offered lso
    ON lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  JOIN subject_offered so
    ON so.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE
    AND so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND so.COURSE_NUMBER = lso.COURSE_NUMBER
    AND so.SUBJECT_ID = lso.SUBJECT_ID
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cc
    ON cc.SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND cc.SUBJECT_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER
    AND cc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
)
SELECT
  ii.display_name AS instructor_name,
  COALESCE(ica.unique_courses_count, 0) AS unique_courses_count,
  COALESCE(iml.total_material_assignments, 0) AS total_material_assignments,
  iml.average_publication_year AS average_publication_year,
  COALESCE(iml.distinct_status_count, 0) AS distinct_status_count
FROM instructor_identity ii
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    kerb,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(COALESCE(subject_label, ''), '||', COALESCE(catalog_number, ''), '||', COALESCE(title, ''))) AS unique_courses_count
  FROM instructor_course_assignments
  GROUP BY kerb
) ica ON ii.kerb = ica.kerb
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    kerb,
    COUNT(*) AS total_material_assignments,
    -- compute average publication year only for numeric years; return NULL if none
    AVG(CAST(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(pub_year, '^(\\s+|\\s+$)', ''), '') AS UNSIGNED)) AS average_publication_year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS distinct_status_count
  FROM instructor_materials_link
  WHERE pub_year IS NOT NULL AND pub_year REGEXP '^[0-9]+$'
  GROUP BY kerb

  UNION ALL

  -- include instructors who have materials but none with numeric pub_year:
  SELECT
    kerb,
    COUNT(*) AS total_material_assignments,
    NULL AS average_publication_year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS distinct_status_count
  FROM instructor_materials_link
  WHERE NOT (pub_year IS NOT NULL AND pub_year REGEXP '^[0-9]+$')
  GROUP BY kerb
) iml_combined ON ii.kerb = iml_combined.kerb
-- The previous UNION ALL can produce multiple rows per kerb (one with numeric years, one without).
-- Aggregate those into final per-instructor metrics:
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    kerb,
    SUM(total_material_assignments) AS total_material_assignments,
    -- prefer the numeric average when present; else NULL
    MAX(average_publication_year) AS average_publication_year,
    SUM(distinct_status_count) AS distinct_status_count
  FROM (
    SELECT * FROM (
      SELECT
        kerb,
        COUNT(*) AS total_material_assignments,
        AVG(CAST(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(pub_year, '^(\\s+|\\s+$)', ''), '') AS UNSIGNED)) AS average_publication_year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS distinct_status_count
      FROM instructor_materials_link
      WHERE pub_year IS NOT NULL AND pub_year REGEXP '^[0-9]+$'
      GROUP BY kerb
    ) t_numeric
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      kerb,
      COUNT(*) AS total_material_assignments,
      NULL AS average_publication_year,
      COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS distinct_status_count
    FROM instructor_materials_link
    WHERE NOT (pub_year IS NOT NULL AND pub_year REGEXP '^[0-9]+$')
    GROUP BY kerb
  ) all_parts
  GROUP BY kerb
) iml ON ii.kerb = iml.kerb
ORDER BY unique_courses_count DESC

rows.question: For each publication year, list the year, the total number of reserved materials, the average length of their titles, distinct number of status, and number of courses, sorted by publication year in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH reserved_materials_non_null_year AS (
  SELECT
    lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS publication_year,
    lrc.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS title,
    -- status should come from library_material_status via material status key in detail, not publisher.
    m.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS material_status_key,
    lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS status,
    -- course identifier comes from library_subject_offered key in detail; use that key as course identifier
    m.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS course_id,
    lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS id
  FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail` m
  JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` lrc
    ON m.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
    ON m.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
  WHERE lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR`) <> ''
)
SELECT
  CAST(publication_year AS SIGNED) AS publication_year,
  COUNT(id) AS total_reserved_materials,
  AVG(CHAR_LENGTH(title)) AS avg_title_length,
  COUNT(DISTINCT status) AS distinct_status_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(TRIM(course_id), '')) AS distinct_course_count
FROM reserved_materials_non_null_year
-- exclude NULL titles from the average by letting CHAR_LENGTH(title) be NULL when title IS NULL;
-- AVG(...) in MySQL ignores NULLs, so above is correct
GROUP BY publication_year
ORDER BY publication_year DESC

rows.question: For each IAP category, list the category name, the sponsor name, the number of activities offered, and the average fee per activity, sorted by the number of activities in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH iap_activity_base AS (
  SELECT
    IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
    IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
    IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID,
    IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR_ID,
    FEE
  FROM iap_subject_detail
  WHERE IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY IS NOT NULL
    AND IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY <> ''
    AND IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY IS NOT NULL
    AND IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY <> ''
    -- treat presence of a session key as indication the activity is offered in IAP
    AND IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
    AND IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY <> ''
),
iap_activity_fees_numeric AS (
  SELECT
    IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
    IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
    FEE,
    -- normalize FEE to numeric: remove $ and commas, treat empty string as NULL, cast when numeric-looking
    CASE
      WHEN FEE IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN TRIM(FEE) = '' THEN NULL
      ELSE
        -- remove common non-numeric characters ($, commas, spaces) then attempt cast;
        -- if resulting string is not a valid number, CAST will produce 0 in some MySQL configs,
        -- so additionally guard with a regexp check to return NULL when not numeric-looking.
        CASE
          WHEN TRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE(FEE, '$', ''), ',', '')) REGEXP '^[-+]?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN CAST(TRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE(FEE, '$', ''), ',', '')) AS DECIMAL(18,2))
          ELSE NULL
        END
    END AS numeric_fee
  FROM iap_subject_detail
),
iap_sponsor AS (
  SELECT
    IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR_ID,
    SPONSOR_NAME
  FROM iap_subject_sponsor
),
iap_category AS (
  SELECT
    IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID,
    IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_NAME
  FROM iap_subject_category
)
SELECT
  c.CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_NAME,
  s.SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  COUNT(*) AS ACTIVITY_COUNT,
  -- AVG over numeric_fee will ignore NULLs; if there are no numeric fees for a category this yields NULL.
  AVG(f.numeric_fee) AS AVG_FEE_PER_ACTIVITY
FROM iap_activity_base ab
JOIN iap_category c
  ON ab.SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID = c.SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID
JOIN iap_sponsor s
  ON ab.SPONSOR_ID = s.SPONSOR_ID
LEFT JOIN iap_activity_fees_numeric f
  ON ab.SUBJECT_ID = f.SUBJECT_ID
  AND ab.SESSION_ID = f.SESSION_ID
GROUP BY
  c.CATEGORY_NAME,
  s.SPONSOR_NAME
ORDER BY
  ACTIVITY_COUNT DESC

rows.question: For each sponsor, list the sponsor name, the number of IAP sessions hosted, and the number of unique subjects organized.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH sponsor_session_subject_pairs AS (
  SELECT
    s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
    sp.SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR,
    -- prefer SUBJECT_ID from schedule when available, else fall back to subject_detail's person key as a subject identifier
    COALESCE(si.SUBJECT_ID, d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY) AS SUBJECT_ID,
    d.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS DETAIL_SESSION_KEY
  FROM iap_subject_session s
  JOIN iap_subject_detail d
    ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp
    ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
  LEFT JOIN subject_iap_schedule si
    ON si.TERM_CODE = d.TERM_CODE
    AND si.SESSION_NUMBER = s.SESSION_SEQUENCE
  WHERE
    -- only include rows that are for the Independent Activities Period.
    -- TERM_CODE commonly contains 'IAP' for IAP terms; filter conservatively using LIKE.
    d.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
    AND UPPER(d.TERM_CODE) LIKE '%IAP%'
    -- only count sponsors with a non-empty name
    AND sp.SPONSOR_NAME IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(sp.SPONSOR_NAME) <> ''
)
SELECT
  SPONSOR AS sponsor_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT SESSION_ID) AS iap_session_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT SUBJECT_ID) AS unique_subject_count
FROM sponsor_session_subject_pairs
GROUP BY SPONSOR
ORDER BY SPONSOR

rows.question: For each person role and IAP category, list the role, the category name, the number of people in this role, and the average fee, sorted by the role count in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH role_iap_persons_fees AS (
  SELECT
    p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS PERSON_ID,
    TRIM(p.PERSON_ROLE) AS ROLE,
    d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
    TRIM(c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME) AS IAP_CATEGORY_NAME,
    d.FEE AS FEE
  FROM iap_subject_person AS p
  JOIN iap_subject_detail AS d
    ON p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
  JOIN iap_subject_category AS c
    ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
  -- Joining sessions is not required for the requested aggregation, so omitted
)
SELECT
  rif.ROLE AS role,
  rif.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS iap_category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT rif.PERSON_ID) AS role_count,
  AVG(CAST(rif.FEE AS DECIMAL(18,2))) AS average_fee
FROM role_iap_persons_fees AS rif
WHERE rif.ROLE IS NOT NULL
  AND rif.ROLE <> ''
  AND rif.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND rif.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME <> ''
  AND rif.FEE IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(rif.FEE) <> ''
  -- ensure FEE is numeric: CAST will fail if non-numeric, so use a safe numeric filter
  AND rif.FEE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
GROUP BY rif.ROLE, rif.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME
ORDER BY role_count DESC

rows.question: List the names of the buildings with the most floors. If there are ties, list each one separately.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_normalized_counter AS (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    BUILDING_NAME,
    BUILDING_COUNTER
  FROM buildings
  WHERE BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL
    -- ensure BUILDING_COUNTER is a valid integer (no fractional part)
    AND BUILDING_COUNTER = CAST(BUILDING_COUNTER AS SIGNED)
),
max_counter AS (
  SELECT MAX(BUILDING_COUNTER) AS max_building_counter
  FROM buildings_normalized_counter
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY
FROM buildings b
JOIN buildings_normalized_counter n ON b.BUILDING_KEY = n.BUILDING_KEY
JOIN max_counter m ON n.BUILDING_COUNTER = m.max_building_counter
ORDER BY b.BUILDING_NAME ASC

rows.question: For subjects offered in the summer term, list the subject titles, number of instructors, and the length of the longest instructor name.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS subject_title,
  CASE
    WHEN so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NULL OR TRIM(so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) = '' THEN 0
    ELSE LENGTH(TRIM(so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME))
         - LENGTH(REPLACE(TRIM(so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME), ',', '')) + 1
  END AS number_of_instructors,
  COALESCE((
    SELECT MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(TRIM(name_part)))
    FROM (
      SELECT
        SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so_inner.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, ',', n.n), ',', -1) AS name_part
      FROM
        (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
         UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
         UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15) AS n
      JOIN subject_offered so_inner
        ON so_inner.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY
      WHERE so_inner.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
        AND n.n <= 1 + (
          LENGTH(so_inner.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME)
          - LENGTH(REPLACE(so_inner.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, ',', ''))
        )
    ) AS split_names
  ), 0) AS length_of_longest_instructor_name
FROM subject_offered so
WHERE RIGHT(so.TERM_CODE, 2) = 'SU'
GROUP BY so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, so.SUBJECT_TITLE, so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME

rows.question: For the mailing list with owner key LIST69.377-keeper-xenon, list the owner, total number of mailing lists, and total number of members across all these mailing lists.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY AS owner_key,
  mlo.OWNER AS owner_name_or_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY) AS total_mailing_lists,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS total_members
FROM moira_list_owner mlo
LEFT JOIN moira_list ml
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY IS NOT NULL -- keep joinable; mailing lists will be counted via detail rows
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail mld
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
WHERE mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = 'LIST69.377-keeper-xenon'
GROUP BY
  mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY,
  mlo.OWNER

rows.question: For each school, list the school name, total number of courses that appear in SIS subject code catalog, and the total number of degree-granting courses that appear in SIS subject code catalog.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  NULLIF(TRIM(s.`SCHOOL_NAME`), '') AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_COURSES_IN_SIS_SUBJECT_CODE_CATALOG,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.`IS_DEGREE_GRANTING` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_DEGREE_GRANTING_COURSES_IN_SIS_SUBJECT_CODE_CATALOG
FROM `sis_course_description` s
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(s.`SCHOOL_NAME`), '') IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY NULLIF(TRIM(s.`SCHOOL_NAME`), '')
ORDER BY NULLIF(TRIM(s.`SCHOOL_NAME`), '')

rows.question: For each department, list the department name, department phone number, number of students, and the length of the longest student full name in that department.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH student_rows AS (
  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT AS DEPT_CODE,
    FULL_NAME
  FROM mit_student_directory
  WHERE STUDENT_YEAR IS NOT NULL
    AND DEPARTMENT IS NOT NULL
    AND FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
),
dept_names AS (
  -- preferred source for department name: student directory's DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- fall back to sis_department.DEPARTMENT_NAME or fac_organization.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
  SELECT
    DISTINCT sr.DEPT_CODE,
    COALESCE(md.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, sr.DEPT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_CODE FROM student_rows) sr
  LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory md
    ON md.DEPARTMENT = sr.DEPT_CODE
  LEFT JOIN sis_department sd
    ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sr.DEPT_CODE
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
    ON fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = sr.DEPT_CODE
),
dept_phone AS (
  -- department-level phone from drupal_employee_directory if available
  SELECT
    HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
    OFFICE_PHONE
  FROM drupal_employee_directory
  WHERE OFFICE_PHONE IS NOT NULL
),
dept_org_map AS (
  -- map DEPT_CODE to an HR_ORG_UNIT_ID if possible using fac_organization or fac_organization.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD
  SELECT
    DISTINCT sr.DEPT_CODE,
    fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_CODE FROM student_rows) sr
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
    ON fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = sr.DEPT_CODE
)
SELECT
  dn.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  dp.OFFICE_PHONE AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE,
  COUNT(sr.FULL_NAME) AS STUDENT_COUNT,
  MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(sr.FULL_NAME)) AS MAX_FULL_NAME_LENGTH
FROM student_rows sr
JOIN dept_names dn
  ON sr.DEPT_CODE = dn.DEPT_CODE
LEFT JOIN dept_org_map dom
  ON sr.DEPT_CODE = dom.DEPT_CODE
LEFT JOIN dept_phone dp
  ON dom.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = dp.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
GROUP BY dn.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dp.OFFICE_PHONE
HAVING COUNT(sr.FULL_NAME) > 0
ORDER BY dn.DEPARTMENT_NAME ASC
